channel.title: Long Island Business News - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Long Island Business News (libn.com)

item.title: LI’s first Toastique to open in Woodbury this month
item.description: Toastique opens its first Long Island restaurant in Woodbury, bringing gourmet toast, cold-pressed juices, smoothies and opening-week specials.

item.title: Big Geyser to host 2026 spring and summer beverage trade show
item.description: Big Geyser’s annual trade show in Uniondale is designed to help clients explore trending non-alcoholic beverages and connect with top brands for spring and summer sales

item.title: Ribbon-cutting for LI’s newest Trader Joe’s
item.description: The new Trader Joe’s opened in a newly constructed building at 300 Route 25A in Miller Place.

item.title: Huntington Arts Council, Reboli launch artist series
item.description: Huntington Arts Council partners with The Reboli Center in Stony Brook for a free 2025 Long Island Grants for the Arts Artist Fellowship series.

item.title: Hooters last Long Island location has closed
item.description: The final Hooters restaurant on Long Island has closed, ending the chain’s local presence after 15 years in Farmingdale.

item.title: Long Island businesses eye cautious growth in 2026
item.description: HIA-LI’s 2026 Business Climate Survey shows Long Island businesses expect cautious growth, citing inflation, AI impact, real estate and interest rates.

item.title: Long Island continues to drive surge in electric vehicles
item.description: Long Island EV ownership grew 23% in 2025 despite federal tax credit cuts, with over 87,000 electric vehicles and expanded charging infrastructure.

item.title: Northwell: Long Island RSV cases drop after vaccination rollout
item.description: Northwell Health reports a sharp drop in Long Island RSV cases and infant hospitalizations following the rollout of RSV vaccines.

item.title: Work starts on long-delayed assisted living project in East Northport
item.description: Sunrise Senior Living has begun site clearing for a $54.6M assisted living and memory care facility in East Northport after a multi-year delay.

item.title: Suffolk launches $600K program for downtown revitalization projects
item.description: Suffolk County offers a $600K Downtown Revitalization Grant Program for municipal capital projects. Applications open Feb. 19; due May 15.
